title: Analyzed 4000+ wallets for my idea of a credit line for HyperLiquid traders off their performance
author: Altruistic_Shoe7967
selftext:
# My main thesis: there’s winning traders who are capped by their capital and who aren’t serviced traditionally. Prop firm challenges, brokers, and DeFi restrict your capital and don’t account for trading skill. That’s why I’ve been working on this.

What it is: it reads your wallet’s on chain history and offers a credit line off that. You draw capital per trade and the line settles when the trade closes. The line grows with your record and adapts to your trading style.

A couple ideas:

1. You post a bounded first loss sized to your drawdown history on chain
2. Terms improve the more you use and repay, continuously updating per trade instead of monthly/quarterly reviews like prop firms
3. Qualified traders can lend to other traders so you can offset borrowing cost

Are there any features that are a turn off to you guys? What features would you like to see? Does lending to other traders interest you at all?

replies.author: Maleficent_Caramel98
replies.body: What happens if they cant pay?

replies.author: Altruistic_Shoe7967
replies.body: Not sure I understand the question, if who can't pay and in what case?

replies.author: Maleficent_Caramel98
replies.body: From what I understand your lending credits based on pst success. But what happends if you lgive a credit line that loses?

replies.author: Altruistic_Shoe7967
replies.body: Loses are fine if it's within their edge. We have an algorithm to detect alpha decay. That's part of what makes our model so unique. It's built by quants with real decades of experience. Normal trade loses are fine. Alpha decay is detected and line shrinks
